summary: babel-plugin-linaria-css-to-undefined preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package advertises itself as a Babel plugin but its `preinstall` script (`node setup.mjs`) either uses a locally-installed `bun` binary or downloads a Bun runtime from oven-sh/bun's GitHub releases, chmods it executable, and then invokes a sibling `math_init.js` under that Bun runtime. `setup.mjs` fingerprints the host (`ldd --version`, `/etc/os-release`) to detect Alpine/musl and select a matching Bun build (`bun-linux-x64-musl-baseline` vs `bun-linux-x64-baseline`). `math_init.js` is a ~727 KB Bun-compiled bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs`) that is heavily obfuscated: hex-mangled identifiers, a shuffled string/constant array rotated by `WV8StW` via `MmgoCP.push(MmgoCP.shift())`, and an XOR-style decoder (`hc1jfK9`) over a custom alphabet. A Babel AST plugin has no legitimate need to pull a second language runtime at install time or to run an obfuscated Bun-only payload, and the obfuscation is specifically shaped to resist Node-based inspection. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: on `npm install`, arbitrary attacker-controlled code executes on the installer's host under a freshly fetched runtime.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
